title: Mitzel v. Hauck — social rides and legal commitment
shortTitle: Mitzel v. Hauck — social rides and legal commitment
summary: The duck-hunting ride example tests whether a social arrangement is a contractual exchange.
notes:
Casebook discussion of a shorter authority.

The casebook uses its setting and the effect of contract classification under the guest-law context to frame the question. The fact that participants share a practical purpose does not itself resolve intention or bargain. The historical guest-law consequence is not presented as a current nationwide rule.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 186–187. Open assigned page 186.
